doom.driver: Strait of Hormuz shipping grinds to a halt ahead of U.S.-Iran ceasefire expiry.
doom.blurb: CEASEFIRE EXPIRES. HORMUZ HOLDS ITS BREATH.
doom.summary: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire is expiring today with, per CNBC, 'no deal in sight' — and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has already ground to a near-halt in anticipation. Meanwhile OpenAI quietly disbanded its preparedness team last month, which is exactly the kind of thing you do when you're very confident nothing could go wrong. On the bright side, Ebola is still getting worse, so at least the multi-front anxiety is consistent.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: U.S.-Iran ceasefire set to expire today with no extension, shipping through Hormuz already collapsing in anticipation of renewed hostilities.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Trump scales back joint military drills with South Korea citing his 'great relationship' with Kim Jong-un, rattling alliance credibility in a nuclear-armed neighborhood.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: OpenAI disbanded its preparedness team — the group tasked with assessing existential model risks — quietly at the end of last month, per the Financial Times.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Ebola in DR Congo is now officially the deadliest outbreak in the country's history, with 2,325+ dead and the Bundibugyo strain spreading faster than any prior outbreak on record.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Anthropic's Claude watermarking controversy and ChatGPT's new Computer History keystroke-tracking feature are drawing scrutiny, but neither constitutes a direct safety failure.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — silhouette composition, deep navy and smoldering orange palette, smoke-filtered light, heavy shadows dominating — a tanker port dispatcher's cramped control booth elevated above an empty Gulf terminal dock, pre-dawn Monday, the eastern horizon bleeding amber-orange through yellowed desert haze, the threatening warmth of a ceasefire expiry dawn pressing through the grimy booth window — in sharp black silhouette against that burning horizon glow, a single heavyset figure sits slumped forward at a cluttered dispatch console, elbows on the desk, head dropped into both hands, the posture of a person watching something collapse in slow motion — the console before them glows with a single monitor, its red downward-trending line graph the only cool light source in the room, casting faint crimson upward onto the underside of the figure's forearms — outside the booth window, the terminal's loading dock stretches into pre-dawn darkness, its massive berths designed for supertankers completely, unnervingly empty, mooring ropes hanging slack into still water, orange bollard lights reflected in undisturbed black water below — no ships, no movement, no wake — the emptiness of the dock is vast and deliberate, the absent vessels implied by the scale of the infrastructure built to receive them — dust particles hang motionless in the amber air, the stillness itself the horror.

dawn.driver: This 10-cent heart drug cuts hospitalizations by 25%.
dawn.blurb: ANCIENT DRUG, MODERN MIRACLE, TEN CENTS A DAY
dawn.summary: In a world grappling with Ebola crises and geopolitical tension, a quiet triumph from medical science deserves a moment: centuries-old digoxin, costing less than a dime daily, can slash heart-failure hospitalizations by a quarter. This isn't a moonshot breakthrough requiring billion-dollar infrastructure — it's an already-available, already-understood medicine being rediscovered for the people who need it most. Accessible, affordable, and effective: sometimes the best news is that the answer was already in the cabinet.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Rediscovering digoxin's power shows that rigorous reanalysis of existing treatments can unlock major gains without starting from scratch.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Cameroon's women footballers won their first-ever Women's Africa Cup of Nations title, a landmark moment for a program that had fallen short three times before.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Jared Kushner held rare direct talks with Hamas leadership in Egypt, a fragile but real diplomatic signal that back-channel dialogue hasn't fully collapsed in Gaza.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: El Niño and Saharan dust are suppressing this year's Atlantic hurricane season, giving coastal communities an unexpected window of relative calm.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A screen-time study tracking Finnish children for eight years found that more screen use correlated with better cognitive processing in teenagers, challenging one of parenting's most entrenched anxieties.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Night scene, all light from artificial sources, deep shadows dominating. The interior of a cluttered Dutch home kitchen at midnight, warm amber glow pooling from a single overhead lamp onto a small wooden table, deep teal darkness swallowing the edges of the room, a lace curtain barely visible at the black window behind. On the table a folded newspaper lies open, its front page dominating the composition, a bold graphic visible on the page showing a tiny pill beside a coin, a downward-sloping graph line rendered in amber and red. Beside the newspaper a single small white pill sits next to a copper-gold 10-cent euro coin, both catching the lamplight, their near-identical sizes unmistakable. A half-empty glass of water glows amber where the light hits it. In the deep background shadow, a foxglove plant in a dark ceramic pot leans against the wall, its purple bell-shaped blooms barely lit by a faint streetlight bleeding orange through the lace curtain. Long shadows rake across the table surface. The mood is quiet, intimate, the stillness of a life-changing fact settling into an ordinary kitchen at the edge of night.
